#### Why each lens ranked it there

_Each lens ranks only the names that passed its own screen, so cohort sizes differ per lens._

##### Cyclical Income — why

The Cyclical Income lens ranked EL.PA 1st of 6 names in its cohort. The lens focuses on dividend yield and payout sustainability within cyclical, capital-intensive businesses. The company's free cash flow grew from EUR 3.21bn in FY2022 to EUR 3.77bn in FY2025 (oldest to newest as stated in the evidence). Net debt of EUR 13.4bn would be repaid in 2.5 years of operating cash flow and 3.6 years of free cash flow. Interest coverage stands at 10.8 times the interest bill. These cash-generation and debt-serviceability metrics underpin the lens's income-sustainability assessment. The Cyclical Income cohort contains 6 names; EL.PA ranked first among them.

##### Magic Formula RAW — why

Magic Formula RAW ranked EL.PA 20th of 21 — a near-bottom placement. This lens screens on earnings yield and return on capital. The ROIC of 5.1% is the capital-return figure that drives the poor ranking; it reflects weak capital efficiency relative to the full 21-name universe. The lens issued a SELL verdict on this basis.

##### Earnings Power Value — why

Earnings Power Value ranked EL.PA 6th of 21 and issued a HOLD. This places the name in the upper third of the cohort on this lens's measures, but not decisively enough to earn a BUY.

##### Quality — why

The Quality lens ranked EL.PA 14th of 21 and issued a HOLD — a below-median placement within the full cohort. The lens's measures of business quality place the name in the lower half of the universe.

The Piotroski F-Score of 5 ranked 16th of 21, below the cohort median. The overall no-concern mark reflects the composite of these three components; the accrual ratio is the strongest individual component.

#### Where the specialists disagree

The voting lenses split: Cyclical Income issued a BUY (1st of 6) while Magic Formula RAW issued a SELL (20th of 21), and Earnings Power Value and Quality both issued HOLDs. That lens split is a fact and is left standing. The specialists also divide. The fundamental specialist is bullish (confidence 0.62), anchoring on the Cyclical Income BUY, the cash-generation record, and the valuation band at the 3rd percentile of EL.PA's own 5-year EV/EBIT range. The sentiment specialist is bullish (confidence 0.68), citing the Armani stake talks, the AI glasses partnership with Meta, and the cash-flow valuation commentary in recent headlines, while noting the next-year EPS forecast trim as a modest headwind. The technical specialist is bearish (confidence 0.72), pointing to a price structure broken across every time horizon: last close of 146.70 sits below both the SMA50 of 155.39 and the SMA200 of 191.47, with a 12-month return of -46.0% and a position -53.2% below the 52-week high. The risk specialist is bearish (confidence 0.68), emphasising the ROIC of 5.1%, the analyst next-year EPS cut from EUR 8.13 to EUR 7.89, the near-bottom Magic Formula RAW ranking, and the debt burden of EUR 13.4bn net of cash against a 3.6-year FCF payback. These disagreements are reported as facts and left standing for the reader to resolve.

_Reported and left standing — the ranker's verdicts are unchanged._

#### Specialist views

**fundamental** — bullish, confidence 0.62
_Is this a good business, and can it keep paying what it pays? Reads the company's own accounts: profitability, cash flow, payout._

The fundamental specialist anchors on the Cyclical Income BUY verdict, citing the free cash flow record (FY2022 EUR 3.21bn through FY2025 EUR 3.77bn, oldest to newest), the 2.5-year operating-cash-flow debt payback, the 10.8 times interest coverage, and the revenue compounding record of +14.6% a year over 5 years and +15.5% over 10 years. The valuation band at the 3rd percentile of EL.PA's own 5-year EV/EBIT range is cited as a meaningful cheapness signal. The specialist acknowledges the ROIC of 5.1% as a material weakness that caused three lenses to exclude the name, the Magic Formula RAW SELL at 20th of 21, and the EPS caution (the 5-year +90.9% rate reflects a trough base; the 10-year rate is +3.5%). Confidence is 0.62, reflecting a solid dividend case offset by a mixed broader picture.

**technical** — bearish, confidence 0.72
_What is the price chart doing? Reads price against its own averages, distance from the 52-week high, volatility. A pullback alone is not bearish._

The technical specialist finds the price structure broken across every time horizon. Last close of 146.70 sits below both the SMA50 of 155.39 and the SMA200 of 191.47. The 12-month return is -46.0%, the 6-month return is -24.6%, and the stock sits -53.2% below its 52-week high — falling over both windows — sustained weakness. Annualised volatility of 30.4% amplifies execution risk. The specialist notes that the Defensive Income lens explicitly cited the 46.0% 12-month fall as a disqualifier, and that the Magic Formula RAW SELL and Earnings Power Value HOLD are consistent with the technical deterioration. The Cyclical Income BUY is acknowledged as a countervailing signal. Confidence is 0.72.

**sentiment** — bullish, confidence 0.68
_What do the news and analysts say? Reads headlines and analyst recommendation counts only. Abstains when no news data exists._

The sentiment specialist reads the 5-item headline set as net positive. Two substantive signals are identified: advanced talks for an Armani stake (strategic optionality) and a headline asserting the stock may be 38% undervalued on cash flow strength (a valuation signal, though unverified against the company's own screening data). A third headline documents AI glasses advancement with Meta. The analyst channel shows current-year EPS essentially flat (EUR 7.22 to EUR 7.24) but next-year EPS cut from EUR 8.13 to EUR 7.89, which the specialist treats as a modest headwind rather than an override. The absence of formal analyst ratings on EODHD is noted. Confidence is 0.68.

**risk** — bearish, confidence 0.68
_What could go wrong? Reads payout stretch, volatility, data-quality flags, anything unverifiable._

The risk specialist identifies three compounding vulnerabilities. First, the price has fallen 46.0% over 12 months and sits -53.2% below its 52-week high, with annualised volatility of 30.4% and a 6-month return of -24.6% — a sustained, multi-horizon deterioration — falling over both windows — sustained weakness. Second, the company owes EUR 13.4bn net of cash, requiring 3.6 years of free cash flow to repay; while interest coverage of 10.8 times appears comfortable, the analyst next-year EPS cut from EUR 8.13 to EUR 7.89 suggests forward earnings power is weakening. Third, the ROIC of 5.1% drives the Magic Formula RAW SELL at 20th of 21 and caused three other lenses to exclude the name — the specialist characterises this as a systemic capital-efficiency problem. The Forensic no-concern mark is noted, but the Piotroski F-Score of 5 ranks 16th of 21 and the Altman Z-Score of 2.32852 ranks 15th of 21 (gray zone). The EPS 5-year CAGR of +90.9% is flagged as carrying an explicit caution about a trough base year; the 10-year rate of +3.5% and EPS growth in only 5 of 10 years are cited as the more representative picture. The Armani stake talks are flagged as introducing potential leverage and integration risk onto a balance sheet already carrying EUR 13.4bn net debt. Confidence is 0.68.

_Specialists inform the commentary only — no specialist can change a verdict._

#### Open questions

- Worth checking: is the Armani stake acquisition being contemplated at a price and on terms that would increase net leverage beyond the current 3.6-year free-cash-flow payback? What are the deal economics, and how would they affect the interest coverage ratio of 10.8 times?
- Worth checking: does the 3-year revenue growth rate of 5.1% (the figure that caused the Growth lens to exclude EL.PA) represent a genuine deceleration from the 5-year rate of +14.6% and the 10-year rate of +15.5%, or is it distorted by a specific base-year effect?
- Worth checking: the Altman Z-Score of 2.32852 sits in the gray zone (between 1.81 and 2.99, below the safe zone of 2.99 and above). Has this score been trending toward or away from the safe zone over recent years?
- Worth checking: the analyst next-year EPS cut from EUR 8.13 to EUR 7.89 — is this cut concentrated in a specific segment or geography, and does it reflect a one-time item or a structural revision to forward earnings power?
- Worth checking: the Cyclical Income BUY is rank 1 of 6 within its peer set. What are the identities and characteristics of the other 5 names in that cohort — are they genuinely comparable cyclical-income businesses, or does EL.PA win a weak field?
- Worth checking: the forward P/E of 20.3 times (this year) and 18.6 times (next year) — how do these compare to the sector median and to EL.PA's own historical forward P/E? The valuation band uses EV/EBIT, not forward P/E, so the two metrics may tell different stories.
- Worth checking: the valuation band reads at the 3rd percentile (cheapest) of EL.PA's own 5-year EV/EBIT range. Does this reflect a genuine mispricing, or does it reflect a market judgment that the earnings power underpinning that historical range has structurally declined — consistent with the ROIC of 5.1% and the analyst forecast cuts?
- Worth checking: free cash flow grew from FY2022 to FY2025 (oldest to newest as stated). At what rate is the FCF-to-net-debt payback period improving or stable over this period, given that net debt stands at EUR 13.4bn?
